content.text: Now I have a clear picture of the issue. The problem is not with Kubernetes itself - it's an application-level bug in the pricing-engine code. Let me update the ticket with my findings.

input.note:
**Root Cause**: The pricing-engine pods are crashing due to an application bug, not a Kubernetes issue. The pod logs show a panic in the pricing-engine code:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3
  at /src/internal/rules/tiers.go:88 in TierTable.Lookup()
```

This occurs while compiling a pricing rule named "BF-2026-STACKED" that has 3 tiers with stacking enabled. The bug is an off-by-one error in the tier lookup logic.

**Evidence**: 
- Both pricing-engine pods are in CrashLoopBackOff status with exit code 2 [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-0]
- Pod logs show the exact panic at /src/internal/rules/tiers.go:88 when compiling the rule
- The image (pricing-engine:4.11.3 deployed 2026-04-27) has not been updated since April, but a pricing rule was likely added or modified around 2pm today that triggers this bug

**Recommended Fix**:
1. Investigate the pricing rule "BF-2026-STACKED" that was added or modified today - this likely changed after the last deployment
2. Either temporarily disable this rule in the pricing-rules-admin or rollback any recent rule changes
3. Fix the off-by-one bug in /src/internal/rules/tiers.go at line 88 in the Lookup method when handling stacked tiers
4. Deploy a new version of pricing-engine with the fix

The pricing-rules-admin pod (which manages rules) is running fine, so the crash is specifically triggered by the new rule configuration it's serving to pricing-engine.
